HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 2366 of 2023
Rajendra Singh ….....Petitioner
 
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ….….Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Mahavir Kohli, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Ganesh Kandpal, Additional C.S.C. for the State
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the 
petitioner is claiming his retiral dues. He retired from the service on 
18.12.2023. But, since then, neither his retiral dues have been paid nor 
pension granted to him. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit 
that due to irregularities in the pay fixation, by the impugned order, the 
petitioner has been directed to deposit certain amount. He would submit 
that insofar as, the pension is concerned, Sub-Committee has already 
been constituted.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the 
record.
3. On being asked, learned State counsel admits that the 
petitioner did not make any misrepresentation or did not play any fraud 
with the system. He is not responsible for any payment that has been 
made to him. But, he would submit that excess payment has been made 
to the petitioner. He also admits that the petitioner is a Driver, a Group C
employee.  2
4. The matter may not be kept pending for all reasons 
indefinitely. The recovery may not be made from a person like the 
petitioner. 
5. In the case of State of Punjab and others Vs. Rafiq Masih, 
(2015) 4 SCC 334, the Hon’ble Supreme Court laid down the guidelines 
on this subject and in para 18 observed as follows:-
“18. It is not possible to postulate all situations of hardship which would 
govern employees on the issue of recovery, where payments have 
mistakenly been made by the employer, in excess of their entitlement. 
Be that as it may, based on the decisions referred to hereinabove, we 
may, as a ready reference, summarise the following few situations, 
wherein recoveries by the employers, would be impermissible in law:
(i) Recovery from the employees belonging to Class III and Class 
IV service (or Group C and Group D service).
(ii) Recovery from the retired employees, or the employees who 
are due to retire within one year, of the order of recovery.
(iii) Recovery from the employees, when the excess payment has 
been made for a period in excess of five years, before the order of 
recovery is issued.
(iv) Recovery in cases where an employee has wrongfully been 
required to discharge duties of a higher post, and has been paid 
accordingly, even though he should have rightfully been required to 
work against an inferior post.
(v) In any other case, where the court arrives at the conclusion, 
that recovery if made from the employee, would be iniquitous or harsh 
or arbitrary to such an extent, as would far outweigh the equitable 
balance of the employer's right to recover.
6. The petitioner is a Driver. A Group C employee, who retired 
in the year 2023. He has not received any retiral dues or pension since 
then. It is a very sorry state of affairs. It is also admitted that the 
petitioner did not make any representation or did not play any fraud.
7. By impugned communication dated 18.12.2023, the 
petitioner has been directed to deposit excess payment in the Treasury. 3
Therefore, the impugned communication dated 18.12.2023 is not in 
accordance with law and it deserves to be set aside.
8. The impugned communication dated 18.12.2023 is set aside 
accordingly.
9. The respondents are directed to pay the gratuity, leave 
encashment and other admitted dues to the petitioner within a period of 
three weeks from today.
10. The respondent no.5, the Executive Engineer, Provincial 
Division, Public Works Department, Pauri, District Pauri Garhwal shall 
ensure it. If it is not made, it shall be construed as his willful 
disobedience. It is stated that with regard to the pension, the Committee 
has already been constituted, which is looking into the matter. In that 
respect, respondents/ State may file a short affidavit within next three 
weeks.
11. List on 20.05.2025. 
(Ravindra Maithani, J)
 03.04.2025
Jitendra

 On 24.02.2025, this Court passed the 
following order:-
 “Meanwhile, the respondents shall 
release the gratuity, which the respondents 
admits to be payable to the petitioner. It 
shall be so paid within four weeks from 
today. If it is not done, the Court would 
initiate stringent action against the 
respondent no.5 Executive Engineer, 
Provincial Division, Public Works 
Department, Pauri, District Pauri Garhwal. 
In case, the respondent no.5 fails, the Court 
shall consider it as his personal failure and 
an appropriate action shall be taken against 
him.”
 Now, a Modification Application has 
been filed. 
 Learned State Counsel would submit 
that, in fact, gratuity has not been 
admitted. 
 Let State file a short affidavit giving 
response to the following:-
(i) Whether gratuity is payable to the 
petitioner? If so, what is the 
amount admitted to the State?
(ii) Why it has not been paid up till 
now?  Let a short affidavit be filed within a 
week.
 List on 18.06.2025, just after fresh 
cases.
